answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them face down; shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five face down on top; shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one face down on top. This makes a 10-card deck: 1 Conflict I, 5 Conflict II, and 4 Conflict III. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In four-player play, a human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, at 0 VP. Each starts with two Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in their garrison and nine troops in supply; and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: score marker is on ‘the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space’; ‘Place two Agents on your Leader’; troops: ‘three in one of the four circular garrisons’ and ‘remaining nine troops in your supply’; ‘Take 1 water.’

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after revealing you are skipped for the rest of the Player Turns phase and cannot take another Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’ and ‘Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Reveal: gain effects ‘of the just-revealed cards only (not of cards played on Agent turns)’; Clean Up moves ‘all cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) to your discard pile.’

answers.answer: No. You must pay destination costs immediately before resolving any effects of the space or the card played, so an Agent-turn card effect cannot first provide resources to pay that entry cost. One card sends only one Agent using one Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: ‘You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents’; costs must be paid ‘immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played)’; ‘A card with no Agent icons can't be played on an Agent turn.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited during the current turn may deploy, plus up to two from the garrison, so at most five can deploy (assuming all three recruited troops are available). At a non-Combat space, you cannot deploy units there; recruited troops go from supply to your garrison. The cube icon recruits a troop from supply into the garrison.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: the cube icon takes a troop ‘from your supply and place[s] it in your garrison’; at a Combat space deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn ... plus up to two more units from your garrison.’

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to enter a space occupied by another player's Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card; choose it immediately after placing your Agent and before receiving space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both effects, though two different Spies can be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent icon access ‘do[es] not recall the Spy’; Gather Intelligence is decided ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects)’; ‘You cannot recall the same Spy to both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.’ FAQ: ‘You may recall two Spies for different effects.’

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm contributes 3, and four revealed swords contribute 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot participate in Combat Intrigue, which is available only to players with at least one unit there.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; ‘if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0.’ Combat Intrigue is for each player with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict.’

answers.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent you from acting again if another player then plays a Combat Intrigue. The window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not their garrison), and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; resolve after ‘all players involved in Combat pass consecutively.’ Cleanup: troops return to ‘supply (not their garrison)’ and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: A tie for first in either a four-player or three-player Conflict means each tied player gets the second reward, nobody wins the Conflict, and nobody takes the Conflict card. In a four-player game, if exactly two tie for first, remaining players compete for the third reward; in a three-player game, no other rewards are given. A player with 0 strength gets no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players ‘each gain the second reward, and no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card’; with three or fewer players, ‘no other rewards are given’; with four, exactly two tied means remaining players compete for third. A player with ‘0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For an optional reward of 3 spice for 1 VP, the doubled reward lets you pay the 3-spice cost a second time to get a second VP: pay 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: ‘If you have one or more sandworms ... double the rewards’; control and battle icons cannot double. For a doubled reward with a cost, ‘you may pay the cost a second time to gain it a second time’; example: pay 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2.

answers.answer: Check for a normal match after winning a Conflict and taking its card into your supply. The matching pair must consist of face-up Conflict or Objective cards with the same Crysknife, Desert Mouse, or Ornithopter icon. Matching is mandatory: flip both cards face down and gain 1 VP. During the Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three types in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the card, check for another ‘face-up Conflict or Objective card’ with the same icon; if so, you ‘must’ flip the pair and gain 1 VP. ‘During the Endgame’ the wild icon can match any of the three.

answers.answer: Reaching 2 Influence gives 1 VP, which is lost if Influence falls below 2. Reaching 4 gives that track space's bonus; it is kept after dropping below 4 and gained again upon reaching 4 again. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP, but merely tying the holder at 4 does not steal it. If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes it; dropping to 3 or lower also loses it, and if no one at 4+ can take it, it returns to the board.
answers.evidence: Scoring: reaching 2 = 1 VP ‘lost if you drop back below 2’; 4 bonus: ‘Keep that bonus if you drop below 4’; tying an existing holder ‘does not steal it.’ FAQ: after holder loses Influence following a tie, the formerly tied player takes it; falling to 3 or lower loses it, and it returns if nobody at 4+ can take it.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent during Reveal before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card or split Persuasion from one source across multiple cards. After buying a Row card, its replacement is available immediately, and an acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal effects: Persuasion may acquire cards ‘before, between, or after’ effects. Acquiring Cards: Persuasion ‘may be pooled’ or split; the Row replacement allows acquisition ‘after acquiring a card’; acquired card goes face up into the discard pile.

answers.answer: At the Makers phase, each unoccupied Maker space (Deep Desert, Hagga Basin, Imperial Basin) gets 1 bonus spice, which can accumulate across rounds; an Agent visiting gains all bonus spice there. A sandworm requires Maker Hooks and cannot be summoned to a Conflict protected by the Shield Wall (Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while the Wall remains). Maker Hooks are a requirement, not spent when summoning. Sandworms are summoned directly into your Conflict quadrant; they can never be placed in a garrison. Removing the Shield Wall permits summoning to any Conflict.
answers.evidence: Makers: an empty Maker space gets 1 spice and ‘this adds to any bonus spice already there’; visiting gains all. Sandworms: Maker Hooks requirement; Shield Wall blocks protected Conflicts; a sandworm is placed in your Conflict and ‘can never be placed in a garrison.’ FAQ says Maker Hooks are retained, not spent.

answers.answer: At Recall, reaching 10 or more VP or emptying the Conflict Deck triggers Endgame at the end of the round. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue, then compare VP. Ties are broken by spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops. If all four remain tied, the FAQ says the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins.
answers.evidence: Recall checks 10+ VP or an empty Conflict Deck. Scoring: ‘At the end of a round’ trigger; first resolve Endgame Intrigue, then highest VP wins. Tiebreak order: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops. FAQ supplies the all-four-tied rule.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup uses 20 contracts: shuffle them, place two face up, and leave 18 face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue cards to the Intrigue Deck and four Imperium cards to the Imperium Deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are left in the box and are not part of standard setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: shuffle 20 contracts, ‘flip two face up’ and place ‘remaining 18 face down’; shuffle 4 additional Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards in; Shaddam is an ‘option’; contrasting-back contracts ‘leave them in the box for standard CHOAM.’

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank. If no contracts remain, the icon gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract is completed by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining at least the shown total spice that turn, including from sources beyond the space itself. The Immediate contract is completed as soon as taken. The Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract is completed when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts: take a face-up contract and replace from bank; ‘If all contracts have been taken ... gives 2 Solari.’ Completion: Harvest requires a Maker space and the shown spice total ‘including from sources other than the space itself’; Immediate on taking; Acquire contract on next acquiring the card.

answers.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract after already sending your Agent to that space this turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held the contract when you sent that Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip the token face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM completion: if the Agent was ‘already sent’ to the space, ‘you must wait until a future turn’; you ‘must have had the contract at the time you sent the Agent.’ Completion means announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply. FAQ reiterates holding it when sending the Agent.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival receives the Ornithopter Objective; the two humans receive the other two eligible Objectives at random, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective starts. First Player alternates only between the humans. The Rival is immediately clockwise from First Player, making turn order First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: ‘Use one shared scoring Rival’; it gets the Ornithopter Objective; two humans receive the other two eligible Objectives, First Player goes to the human whose card shows it; turn order is listed; Rival ‘never takes a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, the Rival ignores it and reveals another Hagal card until it can place an Agent on an unoccupied indicated space. A Place Spy card places a Spy at an empty post of its specified type, or ignores placement if none exists; either way, the Rival reveals another card because it has not sent an Agent. It ignores normal destination costs and effects, applying only the Hagal card's effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Agent turns: ‘Ignore an occupied destination and reveal again’; Place Spy uses an empty specified post or ignores placement, and either way reveals another card. ‘Ignore normal space costs and effects: apply only the revealed House Hagal effects.’ If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, ‘immediately reshuffle it and continue.’
